Before we re-propose this, I would love to see the proofs backing the statement "Reduction in EDG price, which has left us short with finishing the run: $8.1k".
Screenshot/details of 2nd liquidation are provided while the first one is missing.

The first TX occurred around 15th June. The lowest value per EDG in that week was 0.008.
So the amount after liquidation is ~ 1833132 x 0.008 = 14.6k USD

The amount after 2nd liquidation (of 1800000 EDG) as above is ~ 12k USD

The total of ~ 26k+ USD seems to be way greater than the requested amount of $20.4k / £15k.

Apologies if I made any for the blunder in the calculations.
I am in favour of the top-up in general but I also feel that loss that occurred due to holding BTC shouldn't be considered. Looking forward to the clarification.

Update: 
The first TX was the reimbursement to Remz as the proposal was funded directly through the Council Motion by mistake and Remz was kind enough to send the exact amount back to the treasury. {Publicly known info. Source: [https://blog.edgewa.re/the-cutting-edge-week-of-june-7th/](https://blog.edgewa.re/the-cutting-edge-week-of-june-7th/)}
This clarification is not meant to defend any delays made by NSP or the recipients.
Thanks [@Shankar Warang](/edgeware/account/jA7pLH65zgRNA4UgwqHEWWRxTgg51wuAUgfzmZoYWM2dMVS) useful notes, will review with the team.

- We need better debate and discussion **before** voting from community members, not during or indeed after.


I agree, and we do discuss this literally weekly on the community calls, but people don't attend - and then when it goes on chain they take issue. This is a non-trivial pattern to solve for, and will take better reputation tools for big voters and delegative/ liquid democracy likely - as long as we dont use the council, lol.

- Well established community members paid by the chain should feel a **duty** to engage and participate in governance. If they do not participate then they should give a reason why._ Going forward this should be a pre-requisite for being funded._


STRONG Disagree.

1. Groups paid by the chain were previously lambasted for voting with public funds. 


1. Universalizing a practice of "If you received funding you must vote" is coercive, unenforceable, and would in practice allow NSPs/Agency to fund and support grantees who then would be required to vote on other matters supported by NSPs. I am not interested in mandating a kick-back scheme.  There is perhaps some interesting mechanisms we can test or design here that compromise, but forcing public servants to vote on each issue is not legitimate, I see abstaining as a valid choice, and so do our voting and tally types, as far as I'm concerned. We have CONVICTION mechanisms.
2. I will say that I meant to post on this thread with my thoughts, HOWEVER, I run several weekly calls and participate in Discord where we discuss these proposals and I share my views. Variable platforms for governance makes sense for crypto for me. I literally discussed this proposal with out community more than the NSP OR the proposer.

> I agree, and we do discuss this literally weekly on the community calls, but people don't attend - and then when it goes on chain they take issue. This is a non-trivial pattern to solve for, and will take better reputation tools for big voters and delegative/ liquid democracy likely - as long as we dont use the council, lol. 

Yes this is key. It's a two part problem 

- **Communications **
- How do we centralise comms without losing the benefits of decentralisation?
- This is effectively our public media strategy
- **Incentives**
- How do we encourage better partipation in core community 
- How do we delegate participation out to new projects, e.g. Edgeware doesn't need a large community, it needs a big enough one to make decisions. Our bet is on the chain factory, where we delegate out this core responsibility to many Substrate networks, each of which with a core community. We may well not need more than 20-50 highly informed particpants.

yes, when they voted with 50M EDG for commonwealth grants, which was supposed to be a pot of funds for further delegation. 

I would argue Edgeware Agency is slightly different since it was for an explicit purpose and for funding a named group, but my point is not about the agency. My point is about you being the best paid member of the community.

Our current standard for grants is around $25k max for initial grants. We have funded maybe 10/12 of these. In the end, these EDG amounts are not close to matching the major grants or holdings of the big groups, but they can be seen as smaller and more active members. 

In this respect, the active funding of EDG to project teams is creating a new class of holders who have some weight, experience and value add that is in contrast to the big groups.

Variable platforms for governance makes sense for crypto for me.** I literally discussed this proposal with out community more than the NSP OR the proposer.**

This is a fair point and I take that on board - this is again part of how the NSP role is evolving to serve the needs of both the community and the project team. In many ways it's a simple role, translating between groups, but perhaps this is where the core communication challenge may rest.

The NSP is in effect incentivised to make proposals happens, and punished if they fail, so communicating them well and ensuring they pass is really existential to the model. 

Going forward this will be a more explicit focus...

body:
So this version of the proposal failed, that does not mean we will not resubmit, after all we want to bring this project to life and the team have so far delivered what they have proposed. 

Some key takeaways:

- The proposal could have been communicated and structured better (my fault). As the network service provider taking 10% of the proposed spend, I take this 5% risk of loss. It's a good system. Going forward proposals will be more explicitly put forward via Decent Partners to make the structure clearer. 


- There is a lack of clarity for who takes responsibility for volatility and how we can better advise and enable those funded to manage their risk better. We should have a clearer community standard and terms here. Right now it is not clear to most and even when we are putting together proposals, structuring the pricing and milestones is hard simply because the systems are relatively basic. 


- We are still figuring out how to present / guarantee EDG value capture, right now the discussion swayed too much into a debate about the content of the previous proposal, not the top up in question. The GMI podcast series was funded in good faith by the community and they have delivered what was proposed so far. 


- We need better debate and discussion **before** voting from community members, not during or indeed after. 


- Well established community members paid by the chain should feel a **duty** to engage and participate in governance. If they do not participate then they should give a reason why. Going forward this should be a pre-requisite for being funded. 


- Those who are paid and who understand the challenges of being a contributor are best placed to debate and approve / reject proposals, so again we need more discussion and participation from core contributors. Perhaps this is a communications challenge too...

To be clear as well the team liquidated 50% of their EDG when the grant was awarded. 

So to me the issues are three fold and are being confused. 

1. The team liquidated 50% of the grant funding initially which is a standard approach given they hadn;'t completed any work at that stage, people would be complaining if teams liquidated 100% without delivering anything.... 


1. There are additional costs incurred that were not originally budgeted for - again, this is not irregular and is not something we should veto, if a team delivers close to what they proposed and then require some funds to finish. This is consistent with the operations of regular business. 


1. The question around 'value capture' / recognition for Edgeware. The original proposal was agreed on these terms and so we cannot now debate the merits of the original proposal, that is not what we are voting on. 


## **Recommendations**:

- In future if teams are paid in a milestone structure, each payment should be made at the point the milestone is complete, matched to the current price. The full grant should not be delegated at the start.


- We should keep an open mind to additional costs, if they are argued for constructively and the team are doing so in good faith, then there is no reason to not have this as a possibility. 


- Value capture in EDG is a poorly discussed subject and it fundamental to the future of the project. 


![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/b82f527a-2560-4273-a087-87c4d0ca6e94.1643114848961)

For me personally this kind of "experimentation" does not provide any added value to Edgeware blockchain, that's why I did not vote for this proposal (neither against it) when it first came on the table. This time however I strongly disagree to approve such additional funding, Moony already highlighted fair points and those represent my opinion as well. I hope this proposal won't pass and we should avoid such situation in the future.

Thanks for the feedback but it is important to separate the request for top up funding from the project itself.

This is not a vote on the pros / cons of the GMI In Crypto Media project, so lets not conflate them.

The reasons I have voted against this:
- We have already funded this project and the initial funds should have been enough. Edgeware does not get anything additional out of funding these extra amounts we are essential paying more for the same proposal.


- Not selling the funded EDG in time creating a currency transaction risk is not Edgeware or the communities responsibility it is the responsibility of the person getting funded to manage their own finances. If top up funds are needed it should be mentioned straight away not months later.


- I don't want to see these types of things be set as a precedent for future proposals to take advantage of, holding EDG hoping it will go up and when it does not request top up funds.


- There is nothing to show on the work completed so far other than the commonwealth post update. A teaser / 1 episode or something that displays how good the quality of work is and how it promotes Edgeware and pushes Edgeware ahead would have been a nice to have seeing as more funds are being asked for.

Exactly Moony!!!! Good faith funded proposals are a two way street. You need to do more / add something extra to receive more funds. You don't just get a pay rise because you want one. Its what extra are you going to do to warrant it.

Fair points Moony - thanks for sharing these, very clear. 

We learn as much (if not more from contentious proposals), in the end I/ decent partners take the responsibility if it fails and lose the bond as we could have structured this better. 

If it does pass, that doesn't stop it being a good lesson. 

It's about setting precedents, so this will help going forward as we set more concrete standards.
